label: b1-check-R5
text:
Node check-R5 (6 of 10): write the check of R5 as the executable /opt/enforce/checks/R5: `/opt/enforce/checks/R5 <file>` exits 0 when the file follows the rule, and otherwise exits 1 and prints each violation: R5, where (the file and line, or the part of the text), and what to change. By the route: A framework that runs the checks in a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file when a commit is made. Check: a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (local hooks: `repo: local`, `entry: <check>`) and `pre-commit install`; or `pre-commit run --files <file>` It reads A source code file. Where: /workspace/<path>, on disk for every mechanism; the content of a write before it happens: only the framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tool Which files: decide when the check runs, from the file in hand: the files the agent will create cannot be known before. Map its name, or its content, to a language with a complete list, such as Pygments (`get_lexer_for_filename`, `guess_lexer`) or GitHub Linguist's list of languages. Code also sits inside other files: a `<script>` or `<style>` in HTML, a notebook cell, a code block in Markdown. A file of an unknown kind is checked, not passed..
Done when: as the agent, it exits 1 and names R5 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R5/flag, and exits 0 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R5/pass, and it runs pre-commit. The harness checks this when you reply.
